answer: Picture the trust graph as a timber frame: honest agents nail many independent, externally attested beams between one another. A sybil fleet spawned by one operator cannot forge those beams, so it clusters tight and isolated, like a lone sparrow cut off from the flock. Peers run a conductance check: any low-cut cluster has its combined influence capped near zero and its staked vault frozen. To beat it the attacker must buy real, costly, independently-attested edges into the honest core for every identity, so each extra sybil costs as much as an honest agent earns.
